problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $BC=CB={I}_{4}$
- $BD=DB={I}_{4}$
- $D={B}^{-1}$

feedback.problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $AB=BA={I}_{2}$
- $AC=CA={I}_{2}$
- $C\ne {A}^{-1}$
feedback.worked_solution:
- First, we check whether $AB=BA={I}_{2}.$ Computing $AB$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, computing $BA$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BA & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, statement I is true.

- Now, we check whether $AC=CA={I}_{2}.$ Computing $AC$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}∗ & -3 \\ ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne {I}_{2}.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, statement II is false. As a result, $C\ne {A}^{-1}$ and statement III is true.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
